votes.reason: 16.2x trailing earnings with EPS up 13.4% is a fair price for a best-in-class bank, and at 1.88% weekly volatility it is the soundest anchor for the capped position.

16.2x trailing is a modest multiple for a profitable, cash-rich biotech whose EPS is still growing (3.0%); its 5.87% weekly volatility is a reason for the smaller weight below JPM, not a reason to drop it.

At 22.2x trailing it is the most expensive name in the draft while its EPS fell 26.1%, and after a 9.68% rise over 12 weeks to near its high there is no margin of safety, so the case rests on the chart and not on the business being cheap.
A durable staple marked down 8.79% over 12 weeks to 16.7x trailing with EPS still growing 6.2% is exactly the cheap-and-sound profile I look for.
18.3x trailing against 45.2% EPS growth is a reasonable price for a sound franchise, and although it sits at its high after an 18.77% run over 12 weeks, nothing in the value table argues against it.
